disposition_reason: Appendix C prints, per element, the minimum, maximum and mean of detected amounts (ppm) for 39 infant cereals and 69 infant/children's snacks (cookies/biscuits, crackers, granola/cereal bars) bought in Halifax in late 2022.

study.design: Government targeted monitoring survey (Children's Food Project 2022)
study.origin: 72 domestic, 75 imported and 54 unspecified-origin products across all 201 samples
study.market: retail stores, Halifax, Nova Scotia, Canada
study.method: Not described beyond ISO/IEC 17025 accredited contract laboratories; total elements
study.qa: ISO/IEC 17025 accredited laboratories; no CRM or recovery reported

findings.material_label: Infant cereal, unspecified grain (Infant food - cereals)
findings.notes: Bought at retail in Halifax, Nova Scotia, November to December 2022; tested as sold (not prepared). ISO/IEC 17025 contract laboratories; method and detection limits not reported. Minimum detected amount (table note b).

unresolved: Snack results are a single category aggregate of cookies/biscuits, crackers and granola/cereal bars; no per-product-type values are printed, so none can be assigned to specific cracker types.

Text states the highest lead (0.196 ppm) was in a gluten-free cracker made with cassava flour, oat flour and tapioca starch, highest cadmium in wheat-based crackers, highest arsenic in rice-based cereals; these are qualitative attributions.
Lead minimum for snacks printed as '00050'; read as 0.0050 ppm per the text.
Detection limits and analytical method not reported.
Yogurt, yogurt beverages and infant formulas were not tested for metals in 2022.
